title: pulse-prefill-sampler-and-quant-prioritizer
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Many tenants have predictable budget envelopes but heterogeneous traffic shapes. Default batching/caching and quantization profiles were static and either underutilized budget (too conservative) or violated latency SLOs (too aggressive). This PR introduces 'Pulse' — a lightweight prefill sampler + quant prioritizer that dynamically suggests tenant-scoped defaults and exposes a dry-run CLI for conservative rollout.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a telemetry adapter that translates per-tenant cost/latency traces into candidate prefill/batching defaults and a ranked set of quantization profiles. The adapter publishes suggestions to the prefill engine via the existing defaults API.
- Implements a Pulse sampler daemon (prefill/pulse_sampler) that runs short synthetic samples against model variants to estimate latency/quality tradeoffs for candidate quant profiles. Sampling is workload-weighted (recent traffic sketches) to avoid noisy signals from tiny routes.
- Adds a prioritizer: a simple scoring function combining unit-econ delta, 99p latency delta, and measured quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE-like or model-specific regression metric) to rank quant candidates.
- Introduces a CLI (rb-pulse dry-run) that operators can use to run deterministic dry-runs against a tenant, producing a report and a suggested defaults bundle. The CLI supports a --simulate flag to run in simulation mode using historical traces.
- Adds end-to-end integration tests and new telemetry dashboards (docs/reference/pulse) and a short playbook for rolling changes.

Why different: Prior PRs autotuned defaults from long-running batch signals. Pulse focuses on rapid, safe exploration: sample small micro-batches across a compact quant grid and present ranked options, not automatic rollouts. It lowers human review overhead with a deterministic report and promotes safe manual adoption.

Design notes:
- Score = w_cost * normalized_cost_savings + w_latency * normalized_99p_latency_change + w_quality * normalized_quality_change. Weights default to (0.5, 0.3, 0.2) but are tenant-configurable.
- Sampling uses shadow-mode requests and does not touch live KV caches. Any candidate that increases 99p latency by >20% is filtered by default.
- Quant profiles tested: [fp16, int8-qweight, int8-qkv, int4-mixed] with fallback to fp16 if quality regressions >2% on the tenant's eval set.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests for scorer, adapter translation logic, and CLI parsing.
- Integration tests that spin up a small local runtime and run 50-sample sketches to validate latency/quality signals.
- E2E smoke on staging that simulates tenant traces using the simulate flag.

Files changed (high level):
- prefill/pulse_sampler/*.py: main sampler, scheduler, local cache of sketches
- telemetry/adapters/pulse_adapter.go: translates spans/metrics into suggestion payloads
- cli/rb_pulse/main.rs: dry-run CLI and simulate flag
- prefill/service_defaults_api.proto: small API addition (SuggestBundle message)
- docs/reference/pulse.md: operator guide and interpretation of reports
- tests/integration/test_pulse_endtoend.py, tests/unit/test_pulse_scorer.py

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy telemetry adapter to staging and enable for a handful of low-risk tenants (opt-in).
2) Run CLI dry-runs and gather operator feedback for 2 weeks.
3) Publish suggested defaults to internal defaults-staging for manual canary adopters.
4) If metrics stable, promote suggestions to defaults-prod as manual commits (no automatic apply).

Backward compatibility: The adapter and CLI are additive. Existing defaults API remains unchanged for consumers. Pulse suggestions are advisory by default (no automatic apply).

Security/privilege: Pulse requires read-only access to tenant traces and read-only access to model eval harness. The CLI requires operator privileges to produce suggestions for other tenants.

Open items / future follow-ups:
- Add soft-automatic-apply mode behind a feature flag for tenants that opt into 'aggressive-econ' experiments.
- Expand quant grid and integrate hardware-backed latency models for faster estimates.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration smoke added
- [x] Docs: operator guide + example report
- [x] Telemetry dashboards (staging)
- [x] Security review (read-only)

Related Linear: ENG-1287 prioritizer design, ENG-1314 CLI and telemetry plumbing.

Supporting artifacts: sample dry-run report for tenant 'acme-pay' is attached to the Linear ticket (ENG-1287).

release_notes: Introduce Pulse: a prefill sampler and quant prioritizer that generates tenant-scoped default suggestions via a dry-run CLI. Advisory-only suggestions, safe-by-default filters (99p latency guard). Adds telemetry adapter, sampler daemon, scorer, integration tests, and operator docs.
